leads.title: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms - Section 15(1)
leads.documents: Constitutional equality guarantee interpreted to protect LGBTQ people from discrimination based on sexual orientation; applies to all laws and government institutions including law enforcement in New Brunswick.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; quoted verbatim as s.15(1) equality clause, in force 1985, cited with Egan v. Canada 1995 interpretation

leads.title: Egan v. Canada, Supreme Court of Canada (1995)
leads.documents: Landmark ruling that sexual orientation is included in Section 15 as an analogous ground, granting equal protection against discrimination nationwide including New Brunswick.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited as 'Egan v Canada' and 'Egan v. Canada' 1995 landmark decision

leads.title: Vriend v Alberta, Supreme Court of Canada (1998)
leads.documents: Held failure of provincial legislature to include sexual orientation in human rights law violates Section 15; basis for requirement that all provinces/territories including New Brunswick explicitly prohibit discrimination.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited as 1998 decision, with follow-up statement that as of 2017 all provinces, territories and federal government include sexual orientation and gender identity

leads.title: Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (Bill C-150)
leads.documents: Federal decriminalization of same-sex sexual activity in private between consenting adults, brought into force June 27, 1969; foundational criminal-law status applicable in New Brunswick.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited as Bill C-150, introduced 1967 by Justice Minister Pierre Trudeau

leads.title: Civil Marriage Act (2005)
leads.documents: Federal law legalizing same-sex marriage nationwide, making Canada fourth country worldwide; establishes marriage equality applicable in New Brunswick.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited as passed July 20, 2005, following 2002-2005 provincial court decisions and 2004 Supreme Court reference

leads.title: Expungement of Historically Unjust Convictions Act
leads.documents: Federal expungement mechanism allowing destruction/removal of judicial records for historically unjust homosexual-act and anal-intercourse (s.159) convictions; enforced via RCMP and Parole Board of Canada.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited as granted royal assent June 21, 2018, French title Loi sur la radiation de condamnations constituant des injustices historiques

leads.title: Canadian Human Rights Act
leads.documents: Federal anti-discrimination law of limited application to federal government and federally regulated workplaces (banks, aviation, inter-provincial transportation); provincial human rights laws cover schools, housing, health care, workplaces in New Brunswick.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited in Division of jurisdiction section contrasting federal vs provincial human rights coverage

leads.title: New Brunswick joint adoption legalization (2008)
leads.documents: Documents family-formation legal status in New Brunswick specifically - joint adoption by same-sex couples legalized in 2008.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited in Adoption paragraph: 'New Brunswick legalized joint adoption in 2008, while Prince Edward Island did so in 2009' - no footnote URL provided in excerpt

leads.title: Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police - Formal Apology December 2020
leads.documents: Institutional enforcement acknowledgment of decades of oppression, institutional bias and human-rights violations against Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer communities; creation of Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Committee.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited as statement issued on International Day of Human Rights 2020, quoted apology text included

leads.title: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau Formal Apology to LGBTQ People - November 28, 2017
leads.documents: Government of Canada parliamentary apology for oppression of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer and two-spirit communities; policy context for expungement and non-recurrence commitment.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited as formal apology in Parliament Nov 28, 2017 with full quoted text
